tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, chain executions, agent runs, prompt versions, and dataset evaluations within LangChain and LangGraph workflows
features: End-to-end tracing of LangChain and LangGraph pipelines
Token usage and latency tracking per run
tools.pricing: Free tier: 5,000 traces/month. Developer: $39/month for 50,000 traces. Plus: $150/month for 500,000 traces. Enterprise: custom pricing. Additional traces billed per usage.
tools.best_for: Teams heavily using LangChain or LangGraph who need deep pipeline tracing, prompt management, and built-in evaluation workflows in a tightly integrated ecosystem

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests and responses, token consumption, costs, latency, error rates, and user-level usage across providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure, and others
features: One-line proxy integration requiring minimal code changes
Real-time cost and token usage dashboards
Request caching to reduce redundant API calls
tools.pricing: Free tier: 10,000 requests/month. Pro: $20/month for 100,000 requests. Growth: $100/month for 1 million requests. Enterprise: custom. Overage charged per 1,000 requests.
tools.best_for: Developers who want quick cost visibility and monitoring with minimal setup overhead, especially those needing caching and rate limiting to directly reduce API spend

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: ML experiments, LLM fine-tuning runs, prompt engineering iterations, model performance metrics, artifacts, and inference costs across the full ML lifecycle
features: Experiment tracking with rich metric visualization
W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Prompt and model versioning via artifact registry
Reports for collaborative analysis and sharing
Integration with major ML frameworks and LLM providers
Online evaluations and guardrails via Weave
tools.pricing: Free tier: 100GB storage, unlimited personal projects. Team: $50/user/month with shared projects. Enterprise: custom pricing. W&B Weave has separate consumption-based pricing.
tools.best_for: ML and AI teams that need comprehensive experiment tracking for fine-tuning and training alongside LLM observability, particularly those with existing W&B workflows

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: LLM and ML model performance in production, including embeddings, retrieval quality, hallucinations, toxicity, prompt-response quality, and data drift over time
features: Phoenix open-source local observability tool included
RAG pipeline evaluation and retrieval tracing
Data drift and model performance monitoring
Integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and OpenTelemetry
tools.pricing: Phoenix: free and open source for local use. Arize AX (cloud): free tier available with limited volume. Pro and Enterprise: custom pricing based on data volume and features. Contact sales for quotes.
tools.best_for: Enterprise teams that need production-grade model monitoring with a focus on quality, safety, and bias detection in addition to cost, especially those running RAG or embedding-heavy workloads

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM application traces, prompt performance, token usage, costs, latency, user sessions, and evaluation scores across any LLM provider or framework
features: Score and evaluation tracking with custom metrics
Dataset creation for testing and benchmarking
Cost attribution by user, session, or feature
SDKs for Python and JS/TS with framework integrations
tools.pricing: Self-hosted: free and open source. Cloud Hobby: free with 50,000 observations/month. Cloud Pro: $59/month for 1 million observations. Team: $499/month. Enterprise: custom pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams that want open-source flexibility and self-hosting control with production-ready cloud options, ideal for privacy-conscious organizations or those wanting to avoid vendor lock-in

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, latency, and errors across frameworks and providers using the OpenTelemetry standard, exporting data to any compatible observability backend
features: Built on OpenTelemetry for vendor-neutral instrumentation
Auto-instrumentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and more
Framework support for LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, and others
Exports to Datadog, Grafana, Jaeger, Langfuse, and any OTLP backend
Minimal code change required via automatic patching
tools.pricing: Open-source SDK: free. Traceloop cloud platform: free tier available. Pro and Enterprise tiers available via Traceloop with custom pricing. Self-export to your own backend incurs no additional cost.
tools.best_for: Engineering teams already invested in OpenTelemetry infrastructure who want standardized LLM observability that sends data to existing backends like Datadog or Grafana without adopting a new platform

cost_tips: Implement semantic caching by storing embeddings of past prompts and returning cached responses for semantically similar queries, which can reduce redundant API calls by 20-40% for applications with repetitive user inputs

Right-size your model selection by routing simpler or lower-stakes tasks to smaller, cheaper models like GPT-4o-mini or Claude Haiku while reserving larger models like GPT-4o or Claude Opus only for complex reasoning tasks that genuinely require them

Optimize prompt design by reducing unnecessary verbosity in system prompts, trimming conversation history with summarization techniques, and using structured output formats to minimize response token counts without sacrificing quality

Set hard budget limits and usage alerts at the provider and observability layer levels, and regularly audit cost attribution by feature or user segment so you can identify and deprecate low-value high-cost workflows before they accumulate significant spend
